key_points.point: The document argues for accelerating capitalist development to provoke a reversal of class relations, viewing this as an engine-apparatus for discovery. It emphasizes that liberation must occur within the evolution of capitalism itself, rather than through a return to past economic models. This aligns with accelerationist goals of using technological growth to transcend current capitalist constraints. The author notes that this process requires careful distinction between acceleration and mere speed.
key_points.verbatim: The process of liberation can only happen by accelerating capitalist development, but—and this is important—without confusing acceleration with speed, because acceleration here has all the characteristics of an engine-apparatus, of an experimental process of discovery and creation within the space of possibilities determined by capitalism itself.
key_points.excerpt_context: Section: Within and Against the Tendency of Capitalism

key_points.point: The document supports the liberation of cognitive labor as a central revolutionary task, arguing that this class is endowed with higher power than traditional industrial labor. It posits that cognitive labor is currently repressed by capitalist command but holds the potential to break the repressive horizon. This aligns with the accelerationist desire to democratize cognitive access and leverage intellectual labor for post-capitalist ends. The author acknowledges that this requires a shift from material to immaterial labor hegemony.
key_points.verbatim: With all due respect to those who still comically believe that revolutionary possibilities must be linked to the revival of the working class of the twentieth century, such a potentiality clarifies that we are still dealing with a class, but a different one, and one endowed with a higher power. It is the class of cognitive labor.
key_points.excerpt_context: Section: Within and Against the Tendency of Capitalism

key_points.point: The author advocates for the reappropriation of fixed capital, including information technologies and abstract cognitive models, by worker-subjects. This is framed as an anthropological transformation where the proletariat masters the tools of capitalist command. From an accelerationist perspective, this is essential for building a new technosocial body. The document notes that this reappropriation is a collective and political act rather than an individual one.
key_points.verbatim: The first element is what I would call the “reappropriation of fixed capital” and the consequent anthropological transformation of the working subject. The second element is sociopolitical: such a new potentiality of our bodies is essentially collective and political.
key_points.excerpt_context: Section: The Reappropriation of Fixed Capital

key_points.point: The document calls for a strong institutional transition to transform abstract knowledge into constituent power for post-capitalist institutions. It rejects horizontalism in favor of planning that converges productive and directional capacities into a network. This aligns with accelerationist intentions to build new, robust institutional frameworks. The author emphasizes that planning the struggle must precede planning production.
key_points.verbatim: Planning is necessary—either before or after the revolutionary leap—in order to transform our abstract knowledge of tendency into the constituent power of postcapitalist and communist institutions to come.
key_points.excerpt_context: Section: Within and Against the Tendency of Capitalism

key_points.point: The document asserts that increasing automation in production processes, including intellectual labor, is the primary driver of the secular crisis of capitalism. It views this as a structural shift rather than a temporary failure. This belief supports the accelerationist view that technological evolution is the central axis of economic change. The author notes that this crisis is a result of capital blocking the potentiality of post-Fordist labor.
key_points.verbatim: What is at the center of the Manifesto is “the increasing automation in production processes,” including the automation of “intellectual labor,” which would explain the secular crisis of capitalism.
key_points.excerpt_context: Section: Introduction

key_points.point: The document promotes a Promethean and humanist politics that embraces scientific utopias and the construction of new worlds. It encourages the use of rational imagination to conceive of barriers against death and life's accidents. This aligns with the accelerationist desire to treat AI and technology as a means to achieve cosmic or civilizational progress. The author acknowledges that this humanism must go beyond the limits of current capitalist society.
key_points.verbatim: A Promethean and humanist politics resounds as well. Such a humanism, however, going beyond the limits imposed by capitalist society, is open to post-human and scientific utopias, reviving the dreams of twentieth-century space exploration or conceiving new impregnable barriers against death and all the accidents of life.
key_points.excerpt_context: Section: An Ecology of New Institutions

key_points.point: The author advocates for developing socio-technological hegemony by reformatting material platforms of production, finance, and logistics toward post-capitalist ends. This requires acquiring the highest techniques employed by capital. This aligns with the accelerationist strategy of using existing infrastructure to build a new future. The author notes that this is a task of maturing productive potentialities to advance a new hegemony.
key_points.verbatim: The Left has to develop socio-technological hegemony—“material platforms of production, finance, logistics, and consumption can and will be reprogrammed and reformatted towards post-capitalist ends.”
key_points.excerpt_context: Section: The Reappropriation of Fixed Capital

key_points.point: The document proposes enforcing drastic reductions in labor time controlled by machines while simultaneously increasing salaries. This is framed as a way to translate labor into recognition of equal participation in collective wealth. This aligns with accelerationist ideas about the post-scarcity economic transition. The author notes that this should be claimed immediately through struggle.
key_points.verbatim: The struggle against algorithmic automation must positively catch the increase of productivity that is determined by it, and then it must enforce drastic reductions of the labor time disciplined or controlled by machines and, at the same time, it must result in consistent and increasingly substantial salary increases.
key_points.excerpt_context: Section: The Currency of the Common and the Refusal of Labor

key_points.point: The document advocates for an 'ecology of organizations' that allows multiple forces to resonate and produce engines of collective decision-making. It rejects sectarianism in favor of a framework that can manage complex institutional transitions. This aligns with the accelerationist goal of building resilient, decentralized organizational structures. The author acknowledges that this is a difficult direction to explore but necessary given the limits of 2011-era movements.
key_points.verbatim: The MAP grasps the opportunity to clarify this by proposing a sort of “ecology of organizations,” insisting on a framework of multiple forces that come into resonance with each other and therefore manage to produce engines of collective decision-making beyond any sectarianism.
key_points.excerpt_context: Section: An Ecology of New Institutions

key_points.point: The author calls for building a new intellectual infrastructure to support ideal projects and the study of new economic models. This is presented as an urgent goal for the current political moment. This aligns with the accelerationist focus on creating the knowledge base for a post-capitalist future. The author notes that this is one of three urgent goals for the movement.
key_points.verbatim: First of all, building a new kind of intellectual infrastructure to support a new ideal project and the study of new economic models.
key_points.excerpt_context: Section: An Ecology of New Institutions

key_points.point: The document emphasizes the need to gain control over adequate means of communication, specifically mass media and social networks. It argues that while these have democratized communication, they remain subjugated to traditional forms. This aligns with the accelerationist strategy of leveraging decentralized networks for strategic dominance. The author notes that focusing resources here is a critical task.
key_points.verbatim: The task becomes one of focusing substantial resources and all the energy possible in order to get our hands on adequate means of communication.
key_points.excerpt_context: Section: An Ecology of New Institutions

key_points.point: The document acknowledges the climate system collapse as a significant global crisis, though it subordinates this to industrial policy and the criticism of capitalist production. From a safetyist perspective, this reflects a recognition of existential-scale threats, even if the document's primary focus is on economic and class-based solutions. The author notes that while climate change is important, it is not the central focus of the manifesto's analysis of capitalism.
key_points.verbatim: There are also none of the shibboleths of contemporary discourse, or rather, only one: the collapse of the planet’s climate system. But while this is important, here it is completely subordinated to industrial policies, and approachable only on the basis of a criticism of those.
key_points.excerpt_context: Section: Introduction

key_points.point: The document explicitly rejects the 'catastrophist' framing of the current crisis, arguing that such views are a misinterpretation of Marx. It advocates for active engagement and acceleration rather than pausing or fearing the future. From a safetyist perspective, this dismissal of catastrophic risk is dangerous, as it ignores the potential for runaway processes. The author argues that fear-based discourse is a paralysis of the political imaginary.
key_points.verbatim: Catastrophism? A misinterpretation of Marx’s notion of the tendency of the rate of profit to fall? I wouldn’t say that.
key_points.excerpt_context: Section: Introduction

key_points.point: The document identifies the current state of the world as a 'cataclysm' and a 'denial of the future,' suggesting an imminent apocalypse. While the author frames this in political and economic terms, the language mirrors safetyist concerns about existential risk. The document argues that this condition cannot be overcome spontaneously. It emphasizes the need for a systematic approach to avoid this collapse.
key_points.verbatim: The “Manifesto for an Accelerationist Politics” (MAP) opens with a broad acknowledgment of the dramatic scenario of the current crisis: Cataclysm. The denial of the future. An imminent apocalypse.
key_points.excerpt_context: Section: Introduction

key_points.point: The document calls for planning as a necessary component of revolutionary transformation, moving away from vertical state command toward network-based convergence. From a safetyist perspective, this highlights the need for governance frameworks to manage complex systems. The author notes that this planning is essential to transform abstract knowledge into constituent power. It acknowledges the difficulty of this task in a heterogeneous environment.
key_points.verbatim: Planning is necessary—either before or after the revolutionary leap—in order to transform our abstract knowledge of tendency into the constituent power of postcapitalist and communist institutions to come.
key_points.excerpt_context: Section: Within and Against the Tendency of Capitalism

key_points.point: The document discusses the power of cognitive labor and its potential to be repressed by capitalist command, noting that it is ontologically valorized but devalorized by disciplinary systems. From a safetyist perspective, this reflects concerns about the agency of advanced systems and the potential for them to be misaligned with human interests. The author emphasizes that this potentiality is a matter of power and organization.
key_points.verbatim: It is the class of cognitive labor. This is the class to liberate, this is the class that has to free itself.
key_points.excerpt_context: Section: Within and Against the Tendency of Capitalism

key_points.point: The document argues for the reappropriation of fixed capital, including complex algorithms and cognitive models, to bring them under communist administration. From a safetyist perspective, this raises questions about the safety and control of such powerful tools once they are reappropriated. The author notes that the use of these models by capital does not make them inherently features of capital, but rather a problem of power.
key_points.verbatim: The use of mathematical models and algorithms by capital does not make them a feature of capital. It is not a problem of mathematics—it is a problem of power.
key_points.excerpt_context: Section: The Reappropriation of Fixed Capital

key_points.point: The document notes that informatization is leading to the complete subsumption of society within capital, with automation acting as the cement of this organization. From a safetyist perspective, this describes a systemic risk where society becomes increasingly dependent on automated, opaque systems. The author argues that this is a higher level of real subsumption than previously experienced.
key_points.verbatim: Productive society appears not only globally informatized, but such a computerized social world is in itself reorganized and automatized according to new criteria in the management of the labor market and new hierarchical parameters in the management of society.
key_points.excerpt_context: Section: The Hegemony of Cooperation

key_points.point: The document highlights the role of logistics in configuring territorial dimensions of capitalist command and establishing hierarchies. From a safetyist perspective, this points to the vulnerability of critical infrastructure to automated control. The author notes that this system of knowledge, or General Intellect, is now central to capitalist command.
key_points.verbatim: Now, if extractive capitalism expands its power of exploitation extensively to any social infrastructure and intensively to any degree of abstraction of the productive machine (at any level of global finance, for instance), it will be necessary to reopen the debate on the reappropriation of fixed capital within such a practical and theoretical space.
key_points.excerpt_context: Section: The Hegemony of Cooperation

key_points.point: The document discusses the production of subjectivity and the agonistic use of passions as a counter to capitalist command. From a safetyist perspective, this emphasizes the importance of human-centric values in the face of automated systems. The author argues that historical dialectics are necessary to oppose sovereign command.
key_points.verbatim: And, at this point, we should not forget to open up another theme: the production of subjectivity, the agonistic use of passions, and the historical dialectics this opens against capitalist and sovereign command.
key_points.excerpt_context: Section: The Currency of the Common and the Refusal of Labor

key_points.point: The document acknowledges that the current cycle of struggles has shown insuperable limits regarding forms of organization when clashing with power. From a safetyist perspective, this reflects the difficulty of governing and controlling complex, decentralized movements. The author notes that despite their strength, these movements lacked proper tools and alternatives.
key_points.verbatim: This is even clearer today, at the end of the cycle of struggles that started in 2011, which have all shown insuperable limits regarding their forms of organization throughout their clashes with power, despite their strength and new genuine revolutionary contents.
key_points.excerpt_context: Section: An Ecology of New Institutions

key_points.point: The document calls for the activation of all possible institutional forms of class power, both transitional and permanent. From a safetyist perspective, this highlights the need for robust governance structures to manage the transition to new systems. The author argues that a unitary constitution of class power is only possible through the hybridization of all experiences.
key_points.verbatim: A unitary constitution of class power will be possible only through the assemblage and hybridization of all experiences developed so far, and those yet to be invented.
key_points.excerpt_context: Section: An Ecology of New Institutions

key_points.point: The document identifies the increasing automation of production and intellectual labor as the cause of the secular crisis of capitalism. This aligns with the skeptic view that AI-driven labor displacement is a measurable, immediate harm. The author notes that this has led to the obstruction of productive capacities and the repression of living labor.
key_points.verbatim: What is at the center of the Manifesto is “the increasing automation in production processes,” including the automation of “intellectual labor,” which would explain the secular crisis of capitalism.
key_points.excerpt_context: Section: Introduction

key_points.point: The document argues for a systematic, class-based approach to building a new economy, focusing on the real, measurable impacts of capitalist command. This aligns with the skeptic preference for targeting evidenced harms over speculative risks. The author criticizes the Left for being deceived by impossible hypotheses like Keynesian resistance.
key_points.verbatim: Only a systematic class-based approach to the construction of a new economy, along with a new political organization of workers, will make possible the reconstruction of hegemony and will put proletarian hands on a possible future.
key_points.excerpt_context: Section: Introduction

key_points.point: The author criticizes the 'horizontal' and 'spontaneous' organizational concepts of contemporary movements, calling them fetishistic determinations of democracy. This aligns with the skeptic critique of movements that lack concrete, actionable alternatives to financial capital. The author notes that these movements have no effectual consequences on the institutions of capitalist command.
key_points.verbatim: The MAP deploys a strong criticism against the “horizontal” and “spontaneous” organizational concepts developed within contemporary movements, and against their understanding of “democracy as process.”
key_points.excerpt_context: Section: Within and Against the Tendency of Capitalism

key_points.point: The document asserts that informatization and automation are reorganizing the labor market and society according to new hierarchical parameters. This aligns with the skeptic concern about the hidden economic costs and structural changes brought by AI. The author notes that this is a higher level of real subsumption of society by capital.
key_points.verbatim: Productive society appears not only globally informatized, but such a computerized social world is in itself reorganized and automatized according to new criteria in the management of the labor market and new hierarchical parameters in the management of society.
key_points.excerpt_context: Section: The Hegemony of Cooperation

key_points.point: The document argues that politics must change to address the new reality of extractive capitalism, where fixed capital is reappropriated by the collectivity. This aligns with the skeptic view that economic and social structures must be reimagined for the AI economy. The author notes that this requires a programmatic indication of how to anticipate the attack on the measure of labor.
key_points.verbatim: The communist program for a postcapitalist future should be carried out on this terrain, not only by advancing the proletarian reappropriation of wealth, but by building a hegemonic power—thus working on “the common” that is at the basis of both the highest extraction/abstraction of value from labor and its universal translation into money.
key_points.excerpt_context: Section: The Currency of the Common and the Refusal of Labor

key_points.point: The author advocates for the 'refusal of labor' as a response to algorithmic automation, calling for drastic reductions in labor time and salary increases. This aligns with the skeptic focus on the social and human-centric impacts of AI. The author notes that this is a way to recognize equal participation in collective wealth.
key_points.verbatim: The struggle against algorithmic automation must positively catch the increase of productivity that is determined by it, and then it must enforce drastic reductions of the labor time disciplined or controlled by machines and, at the same time, it must result in consistent and increasingly substantial salary increases.
key_points.excerpt_context: Section: The Currency of the Common and the Refusal of Labor

key_points.point: The document notes that the cycle of struggles since 2011 has shown insuperable limits regarding organization, despite their strength. This aligns with the skeptic observation of patterns in tech adoption and the failure of spontaneous movements to achieve lasting change. The author argues that these movements lacked proper tools and alternatives.
key_points.verbatim: This is even clearer today, at the end of the cycle of struggles that started in 2011, which have all shown insuperable limits regarding their forms of organization throughout their clashes with power, despite their strength and new genuine revolutionary contents.
key_points.excerpt_context: Section: An Ecology of New Institutions

key_points.point: The document calls for focusing resources on adequate means of communication, arguing that current social networks remain subjugated to traditional forms. This aligns with the skeptic focus on real, present problems rather than speculative ones. The author notes that this is a critical task for the movement.
key_points.verbatim: The task becomes one of focusing substantial resources and all the energy possible in order to get our hands on adequate means of communication.
key_points.excerpt_context: Section: An Ecology of New Institutions

key_points.point: The document asserts that money functions as an abstract machine for measuring value extracted from society. This aligns with the skeptic concern about AI's impact on law and accountability, particularly in financial services. The author notes that this monetary abstraction points to potential forms of resistance.
key_points.verbatim: The authors of the Manifesto are well aware that today, money has the particular function—as an abstract machine—of being the supreme form of measurement of the value extracted from society through the real subsumption of this current society by capital.
key_points.excerpt_context: Section: The Currency of the Common and the Refusal of Labor

key_points.point: The document proposes building a new intellectual infrastructure to support ideal projects and the study of new economic models. This aligns with the skeptic intention to reimagine economic and social structures for the AI era. The author notes that this is an urgent goal for the movement.
key_points.verbatim: First of all, building a new kind of intellectual infrastructure to support a new ideal project and the study of new economic models.
key_points.excerpt_context: Section: An Ecology of New Institutions

key_points.point: The author argues that the struggle against algorithmic automation must result in a base income to recognize equal participation in collective wealth. This aligns with the skeptic intention to address the labor market impacts of AI through social policy. The author notes that this is a way to increase individual joie de vivre.
key_points.verbatim: On the other hand, a base income must be instituted so as to translate any figure of labor into the recognition of the equal participation of all in the construction of collective wealth.
key_points.excerpt_context: Section: The Currency of the Common and the Refusal of Labor

factual_claims.claim: The Manifesto for an Accelerationist Politics (MAP) was published in 2013 by Alex Williams and Nick Srnicek.
The cycle of struggles that started in 2011 showed insuperable limits regarding their forms of organization.
The expression 'One divides into Two' originated in Maoist China in the 1960s.
Mario Tronti introduced the concept of the 'social factory' in 1962.
The tendency of the rate of profit to fall is described in Karl Marx's Capital, volume 3, chapter 13.
The sum total of mechanical forces exerted by isolated workers differs from the social force developed when many hands cooperate.
The Manifesto for an Accelerationist Politics (MAP) was written in 2013.

unmapped_concepts.suggested_description: An intention within accelerationist discourse that prioritizes the acquisition of capitalist technical and organizational tools to build a new, post-capitalist power structure. Encompasses: reprogramming logistics, finance, and communication platforms. Excludes: traditional horizontalist or spontaneous movement strategies.
unmapped_concepts.concept: The document argues that the Left must develop socio-technological hegemony by reformatting material platforms of production and logistics. It posits that these tools are not inherently capitalist but are currently repressed by capitalist command. By reappropriating these tools, the proletariat can build a new, post-capitalist administration.
unmapped_concepts.reason: This concept describes a specific strategic approach to institutional transition that is not fully captured by existing nodes.

unmapped_concepts.suggested_description: A belief within accelerationist discourse that distinguishes between traditional labor exploitation and the broader extraction of value from social infrastructure. Encompasses: social knowledge, logistics, and financial abstraction. Excludes: narrow definitions of factory-based labor exploitation.
unmapped_concepts.concept: The document posits that capital now exploits society extensively through social infrastructure and intensively through abstraction. It argues that fixed capital is now primarily established in the surplus produced by social cooperation, which is incommensurable and beyond the sum of individual labor.
unmapped_concepts.reason: This distinction is central to the document's analysis of modern capitalism and its potential for reappropriation.

unmapped_concepts.suggested_description:
A situation concept that describes a framework of multiple, resonant forces working together to produce collective decision-making engines. 
Encompasses: hybridization of political and unionist experiences, resonance between local and global struggles. 
Excludes: sectarianism, vertical state command, and extremist horizontalism.
unmapped_concepts.concept: The document proposes an 'ecology of organizations' to overcome the limits of spontaneous movements. It suggests that multiple forces can come into resonance to manage collective decision-making without falling into the traps of centralism or horizontalism. This framework is presented as a necessary evolution for revolutionary transformation.
unmapped_concepts.reason: This concept provides a specific organizational model that is distinct from existing taxonomy nodes.
unmapped_concepts.Accelerationist Interpretation: Accelerationists would view this as a necessary evolution of organizational form, allowing for the scaling of revolutionary power through network-based resonance.
unmapped_concepts.Safetyist Interpretation: Safetyists might view this as a complex, potentially unstable system that requires robust governance to prevent unintended consequences or power-seeking behavior.
unmapped_concepts.Skeptic Interpretation: Skeptics would likely view this as a theoretical construct that fails to address the practical, organizational hurdles faced by real-world movements.
